name: the keys-off mark is never set
why: Without data-mbu-keys-off Event Horizon's u, Ctrl+P and player keys act on our table (the state before C3 was adopted).
grep: the marks go up with the table

name: the render tail does not sync the marks
why: _mbuTableShown() is where a render reports the table; without the call the marks never go up.
grep: the marks go up with the table

name: keys-keep is never set (V dies)
why: data-mbu-keys-off alone suspends EVERY Event Horizon command, its on/off switch included: the user is locked out of Event Horizon on our table.
grep: V toggles with the marks set

name: the letter guard is not skipped under the marks
why: EH exempts the view COMMAND whatever its key; our capture-phase letter list would still swallow a toggle rebound to h.

name: the String Theory version gate is removed
why: An Event Horizon that honours keys-off but not keys-keep (String Theory 2026.11.20.164048, or a standalone EH) would lose V under the marks.

name: the version compare accepts any version
why: A compare that returns true on the first differing number lets 2026.11.20.164048 through: marks under an EH without keys-keep.

name: the marks stay up in Event Horizon's view
why: In its own view EH's keys are its own; the marks there would suspend all of them but V.
grep: V toggles with the marks set

name: the observer does not sync the marks
why: Without the <html> observer's call the marks do not follow Event Horizon's view coming and going.
grep: V toggles with the marks set

name: another script's keys-off is removed
why: The protocol: a mark is removed only while its value is still ours.

name: another script's keys-off is overwritten
why: The protocol: a mark is set only when absent; the value names its owner.

name: a keys-keep without toggle is ignored
why: Beside someone else's keys-keep that lacks the toggle token, our keys-off would take V.

name: u is missing from the letter list
why: EH's u (your profile, since 0693aea) leaves the page wherever the marks are not up: the initial page, a standalone EH, an older String Theory.

name: the setting is ignored by the marks
why: sa_block_eh_single_keys off must give Event Horizon all its keys back, the marks included.

name: a standalone Event Horizon's data-mbu-eh is not read
why: Only String Theory's mark counts: a standalone Event Horizon keeps the letter guard, so u is guarded but Ctrl+P and its player keys act on our table, and a toggle rebound to a listed letter is swallowed.
grep: standalone Event Horizon with its version mark

name: any data-mbu-eh counts, whatever its version
why: The floor keeps out an Event Horizon whose keys-off would take V; a mere presence check sets the marks over it.

name: the <html> observer does not watch data-mbu-eh
why: Event Horizon writes its mark at its own start, which can come after our render; then the marks would wait for the next render.
grep: Event Horizon.s mark set after the render

name: the <html> observer does not watch data-mbu-st
why: String Theory writes its mark at its start too; a late one would wait for the next render.
grep: String Theory.s mark set after the render
